feed.title: MHFE: memory-hard encryption of BIP39 backups into 24 words — request for review

entry.title: MHFE: memory-hard encryption of BIP39 backups into 24 words — request for review
entry.summary:
MHFE (Memory-Hard Feistel Encryption) is an experimental encryption specification designed to secure English BIP39 mnemonics using a password, converting them into another 24-word, checksum-valid BIP39 mnemonic known as the container. This system is particularly aimed at enhancing the security of offline cold-storage backups like metal plates and capsules. Crucially, when recovering the original mnemonic, no funds are moved, and the wallet remains unchanged, with any pre-existing BIP39 passphrase being reapplied post-recovery just as before.
The technical foundation of MHFE involves a 12-round balanced Feistel permutation where each round utilizes Argon2id with a state-derived salt to ensure robust security. The settings default to 2 GiB of memory, 12 passes, and four lanes per call, with each of the twelve sequential calls reusing memory. This design choice makes the recovery process intentionally resource-intensive, taking approximately one to two minutes on a reference laptop, thereby enhancing security against unauthorized access. It is essential that passwords are strong and independently generated to maximize the effectiveness of these security measures.
One innovative aspect of MHFE is its efficient use of mnemonic length variations. Depending on the length of the original mnemonic, the corresponding entropy and recovery verifier bits differ, allowing the entire 256-bit state of the container to be fully utilized without requiring additional backup words. For instance, a 12-word source results in 128 bits of source entropy plus a 128-bit recovery verifier. This structured variability not only optimizes space but also offers two distinct configurations for wallet creation: opting for a shorter original mnemonic with an internal recovery check or a full 24-word mnemonic dedicated entirely to entropy.
Additionally, MHFE supports plausible deniability through the creation of decoy wallets. By decrypting the container with an alternative password, users can generate a different yet valid mnemonic, which can be pre-funded and used as a functional decoy. This feature allows for credible deniability even if the use of MHFE is disclosed under duress, although it relies heavily on the secrecy of the original mnemonic's length and other conditions outlined in the supplementary documents hosted on [GitHub](https://github.com/hobby-eng/mhfe-spec/blob/main/docs/DESIGN-NOTES.md).
The project documentation and reference implementations are available on GitHub, providing detailed design analysis, test vectors, and an independent OpenSSL-based verification script. These resources are crucial for developers and cryptography experts who may wish to review or contribute to the further development of MHFE. Feedback is particularly sought on areas such as cryptanalysis, plausible deniability, and recovery interoperability, with the aim of refining the specification to better meet the needs of wallet developers and users.
This encryption approach remains experimental and lacks independent expert cryptographic review, highlighting the importance of community feedback and technical scrutiny in its ongoing development.
